speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Senior Minister of State Sun will provide more details.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: If all goes well, I intend to trial AVs in other parts of Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We are considering Sentosa, Tuas and Mandai, amongst others, as possibilities.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This will depend on whether there is interest from AV companies and commuters in these areas.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But for technological and commercial reasons, autonomous buses are developing more slowly than autonomous cars.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So, we will continue to watch this space closely.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: AVs are just one part of our future transport landscape.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We are putting together our next Land Transport Masterplan now.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And in developing this plan, there are many exciting things we want to share and we also want to hear from Singaporeans to understand your transport needs and co-create ideas on how we can address these needs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Minister of State Baey Yam Keng has been leading this effort.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We hope to hear from more in the coming months, as we intensify our public engagements.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: On public transport, one common feedback is long travel times, especially from HDB estates further away from the city.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our upcoming MRT lines like the Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line will bring us closer to this goal.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We will also need to improve the bus network, and first- and last-mile connectivity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: To Mr Andre Low’s suggestion on express train lines, express services can reduce travel time by a bit for some commuters, because Singapore is small.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But typically, they require a separate set of tracks and additional signalling systems.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And this means much more significant land take, much higher costs and more time needed for construction.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Skip-stop services, which are essentially sharing tracks for express and regular services, are technically possible, but this is operationally complex and regular trains have to be held back at stations to allow express trains to pass.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This will have significant adverse impact for commuters on regular services.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We will keep an eye on this issue.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: If the technology improves, we will consider it.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But for the Seletar Line, I think it is unlikely that we will implement it.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Another frequently raised topic is train crowding, and Mr Low spoke about the NEL – in a slightly overstated fashion, I think.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In the longer term, new MRT connections like the Cross Island Line and the Seletar Line will improve the situation for residents in the North-East.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But in the short term, I have brought back free morning off-peak travel on the NEL and Sengkang-Punggol LRT, to encourage more commuters to shift out of the morning peak.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It is early days yet because we implemented it at the turn of the year, but I am happy to share that this has so far been quite effective.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The crowdedness has come down, akin to the effect of adding two extra trains, or 20 buses.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: A third popular topic is whether we can add more bus services.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I received many such requests, including two in the last half an hour in this Chamber, which I have noted – Flora Drive and Compassvale Crescent.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: My MOT colleagues and LTA have been trying our very best.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I would very much like to launch more bus services.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: To do so, I need to buy buses.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I also need to build depots and interchanges, including in Sungei Serangoon.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But most importantly, I need to hire bus captains.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: There are just not enough Singaporeans who want to be bus drivers and we have already reached the limit in terms of how many foreign bus drivers we can recruit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling proposed raising the starting salary for bus captains, which is now around $3,600, including overtime, to attract new recruits.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: We are in discussions with the bus operators and the National Transport Workers' Union on this as well as to further improve working conditions and career progression for existing bus captains.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: A fourth area we receive a lot of feedback on is COEs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Edward Chia asked if we will review the COE system, given new developments, such as EVs, AVs and the ERP 2.0 system.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: The COE system was introduced in 1990 to control our vehicle population as we do not have enough land in Singapore for every person or even every household to own a car.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: If every household owns a car, we would have around 1.5 million cars on our roads – more than double our current car population.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our roads will be jammed up, like in many cities around the world, during peak hours and also off peak.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Every vehicle takes up road space and contributes to congestion, including motorcycles.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This is why, to Mr Azhar Othman's query, we cannot exclude motorcycles from our COE system.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mr Edward Chia has observed that the recent Category A and B prices have converged.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This is not the first time this has happened.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In 2014, we added a power rating criterion to engine capacity precisely to separate Category A and Category B cars more clearly.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This was in response to public feedback that Category A and B cars were becoming indistinguishable because there were more cars with smaller engine capacities but higher power.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But as Mr Chia pointed out, in recent years, manufacturers have been adjusting specifications of cars to fit within Category A.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: This has once again caused Category A and B prices to converge.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I hope Members can see from the above examples how MOT listens to feedback and tries our hardest to address concerns.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: However, in land transport, many issues are zero sum.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: There is a trade-off for almost every decision we make and therefore, someone who is upset if he or she feels that they are on the wrong side of the line.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: An example is bus route planning, which Ms Valerie Lee and Mr Abdul Muhaimin asked about.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: LTA's bus planners are trained, when planning routes, to take into account current and future ridership – not just current ridership but also future ridership – journey times, travel patterns, alternative routes, amongst others.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: They are professionals, but even they find it very difficult, almost impossible, to satisfy everyone's preferences despite their best efforts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Residents in one part of my division have been asking why a particular popular bus service did not stop at one bus stop downstairs from their homes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: After further analysis, LTA found that it was indeed possible to adjust the route.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: After the adjustment, most of the residents in those HDB blocks were very happy.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: But almost immediately, LTA and I got many emails from other commuters complaining that their journey was now longer and the buses were more crowded because of this one additional stop.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I understand that as commuters, we each have our specific personal situations and needs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Mr Chairman, I have shared how we will remain globally oriented, plan for the future and put people at the centre of what we do.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: And when I say people, I do not mean just the commuters.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: I also mean our transport workers who are the heart of my team.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Over the last nine months, I have met many of them over meals, festive celebrations and award ceremonies.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our rail maintenance workers toil in the quiet hours of the night.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our seafarers spend months away from their families.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Our air traffic controllers keep their heads cool in high-stress environments.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: These are but a few examples in our family of over 300,000 transport workers.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Their work is unseen and unheard, but they are the ones who keep us moving and they will always have my support.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: In August last year, I met Hasri Bin Abiden at Tengah bus interchange.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: He has been a bus captain for over 10 years.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: When a new bus service was introduced recently, Hasri volunteered to take on this new route.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: For an experienced bus captain, this is a challenge.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: It means changing routines and dealing with unfamiliar surroundings.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Hasri told me that before he was deployed, he decided on his own accord to get on his motorcycle and practise the route all by himself at night, for many nights.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: He wanted to familiarise himself with the route so that he could better serve his future passengers.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: Every morning, he and many like him try to be the best that they can because they are proud of what they do.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
text: So that tomorrow morning and every morning after that, Singaporeans can step out of our homes with the confidence to get to where we want to go.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I will respond to Members on air and land transport issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are focused on building a globally oriented, future-focussed and people-centric transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Singapore's aviation story is one of constant evolution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: From a small island nation, we have built one of the world's most interconnected air hubs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are now linked to over 170 cities around the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, being a hub also means we are not immune to global disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are monitoring the Middle East conflict closely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The safety of flights and passengers remain our top priority.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Other airlines that fly to Middle Eastern destinations from Changi have also cancelled or delayed their flights.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But even as we navigate the global climate of uncertainty, we never lose sight of the longer-term horizon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over the next decade, we expect Changi to continue to grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our growth thus far has also created over 60,000 quality jobs directly in aviation, from air traffic controllers managing our busy skies to engineers managing our aircrafts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: By 2040, global air travel demand is set to double and Asia Pacific will be driving two thirds of this growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are already preparing our infrastructure to support this by building T5.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The growth of Changi will bring about more opportunities for all, including good, well-paying jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked how we are investing in our aviation workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over the past six months, CAAS has consulted extensively with aviation companies, schools, unions and workers to understand how to help Singaporeans access quality jobs in the aviation industry and progress in their careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, CAAS will work with our IHLs to integrate professional training and undergraduate education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The aviation industry offers many rewarding and well-paying careers, such as in air traffic control and aircraft engineering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have a good pipeline of IHL students who are training for such roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes Wong Rui Qi, who is currently pursuing a diploma in Aerospace Engineering at Temasek Polytechnic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Rui Qi shared with me about his interest in aerospace engineering and his eagerness to start a career as a licensed aircraft engineer as soon as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: By embedding industry-recognised skills training into the IHL curriculum, students, like Rui Qi, will be able to graduate more job-ready and embark on their aviation careers quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, CAAS will enhance the workplace environment and experience for the Changi workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This could include enhancing our infrastructure, improving transport accessibility to and from the airport, particularly during late and early hours, and also providing better rest facilities for workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, CAAS will work with NTUC to develop a sector-wide mentorship scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will support the career development of new entrants to the aviation workforce in key operational roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will enable us to build a future-ready and resilient next generation of aviation professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: CAAS will share more details for each of these three areas in the coming year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To complement these efforts, we are also strengthening our outreach to bring aviation opportunities closer to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Last Saturday, I attended the East Side OneAviation Careers Fair at Heartbeat@Bedok.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There were over 2,000 job vacancies available in the aviation and aerospace sector and 18 participating organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I look forward to working with interested Community Development Councils (CDCs) to bring aviation and aerospace careers to more local communities in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I look forward to working with interested CDCs to bring aviation and aerospace careers to more local communities in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Poh Li San asked about how we are attracting women to join the aviation sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I recently met Ms Megan Zheng, who has been an air traffic control officer (ATCO) for the past 12 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: She shared that it is a job like no other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Other than it being deeply fulfilling, she knows that every instruction that she gives helps guide an aircraft safely to land and that she is responsible for the lives of all the passengers and crew on board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And while ATCOs work shifts, Megan explained that her rosters are planned well in advance, up to a year ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And this allows officers like herself with two young children to plan their family commitments and personal time with confidence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As our air traffic continues to grow, we look forward to having more ATCOs join us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond the skies, the way that we run our airport is also evolving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Autonomous wheelchairs are also being trialled in T2 to help us meet the changing mobility needs of our passengers in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is the exciting future that draws in our students like Ms Ng Yu Jing from Temasek Polytechnic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Yu Jing and her course mates shared with me their enthusiasm to be a part of T5, and to chart the next chapter of Singapore’s aviation story.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Efforts to attract women into aviation do not just rest with the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When I attended the Women In Aviation Singapore Chapter Gala last year, I was heartened to see women and companies leaning forward to provide opportunities for women at every level in aviation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes the Women In Aviation Singapore Chapter mentorship programme, which gives young mentees access to valuable perspectives beyond their organisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: CAAS has also been working closely with Women In Aviation Singapore Chapter to conduct outreach efforts to girls in schools and young women just starting out on their careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are excited for more women to join our aviation sector, especially as we continue to face manpower shortages and there are many well-paying jobs available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The OneAviation workforce will continue to remain at the forefront as our aviation sector continues to grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are ensuring that our public transport network remains accessible and convenient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The sustainable, long-term solution is to leverage technology, such as AVs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked for an update on the autonomous shuttle operations in Punggol, the AV regulatory framework and support for the manpower transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Many commented that the rides were smooth and comfortable, and 99% said they would recommend the service to others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The shuttles provide last-mile connections not previously provided by direct transport links and reduce travel disruptions by up to 15 minutes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Punggol residents have seen the shuttles making their rounds and told me they are excited to try it soon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The rides will be accompanied with a commentary on features of the AV, and they will be free for an initial period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will allow more people to experience the technology and provide feedback for the operator to improve its service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Grab, the operator, will share more details on how to register for the rides.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ComfortDelGro’s autonomous shuttles on Route 2 in Punggol are making good progress in familiarisation and we look forward to commencing by-invite rides for Route 2 soon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On my rounds in Punggol, I spoke with safety operators on board our autonomous shuttles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Victor Tan has been a taxi driver and a driving instructor with ComfortDelGro for the past 15 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He shared that training to be a safety operator on board the autonomous shuttle allowed him to augment his driving experience so that man and machine operate seamlessly as one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Vincent Teo and Ms Sarah Binte Ahmad wanted to try something new after driving for several years and see the new technology in action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They worked hard for their safety operator training with GrabAcademy and WeRide, which required a 90% passing score.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I hear that Sarah’s four children are incredibly proud of their cool mom and Vincent will be progressing to an AV remote operator course soon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These are examples of fellow taxi and private hire vehicle drivers who are giving autonomous technology a try.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And new jobs will not just be in the area of safety operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There will be new jobs for more individualised in-person customer service which cannot be provided by a machine.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There will be new jobs in maintenance and operations of autonomous fleets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These are better paying jobs of the future that not only our current drivers can consider, but also our younger generation who may be interested in the future of autonomy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is an evolving space and many other countries, like China, Japan, the United Arab Emirates and the United States, are deploying AVs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our best strategy is to prepare our people, our infrastructure and our laws.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As the Prime Minister mentioned, we will make sure that autonomous technology and AI work for us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Together with our unions, we are developing training and conversion programmes for our drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are mapping out new job roles and opportunities for our drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I understand that the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) is having engagement sessions on AVs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: So, a shoutout – if you are curious to find out more, please sign up!

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also developing a more holistic legal framework for AVs, which will specify clearly the responsibilities and accountability of key parties in the ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will provide clarity to our workers, industry and the public, and we will consult each of these groups in the coming year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also leveraging technology for a cleaner living environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our air quality will improve, our children no longer have to breathe in harmful fumes from vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Chua and Ms Tin Pei Ling asked whether our EV charger network is adequate to support the growing EV fleet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am pleased to share that there are more than 29,000 charging points island-wide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have achieved our target to provide all HDB residents with convenient access to a charger, with more than 90% of HDB carparks equipped with slow chargers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This addresses the needs of residents who want to charge their cars overnight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are more EV models that now support faster charging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: New ultra-fast chargers that can add hundreds of kilometres of range to EVs in under 10 minutes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And there are also more sophisticated grid management solutions which allow us to reduce costly infrastructure upgrades.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We envision a mix of charging options to serve different preferences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: EV owners who prefer overnight charging can continue to use the slow charging points near your homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Those who prefer to charge while running errands for one to two hours can do so at a fast-charging hub, with multiple fast charging points of power ratings of around 50 kW.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And those who would like a quick charge of 10 to 20 minutes, similar to the experience at petrol kiosks today, can do so at ultra-fast charging points above 150 kW.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will start in areas with higher EV charging demand and adequate electrical capacity, such as carparks near Compass One in Sengkang, MacPherson market and Plantation Plaza in Tengah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also working with industry to explore ultra-fast charging options and agencies to optimise our electrical grid for our growing charging needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOT’s National Transport Academy, SkillsFuture Singapore and the Institution of Engineers, Singapore will launch a Skills Pathway for EV Technical Specialists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This charts out the progression roadmap for a career in EV maintenance, including the training available from IHLs, the Singapore Bus Academy and NTUC LearningHub.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Major automotive employers, such as Borneo Motors, BYD, Cycle & Carriage and Komoco, and our public bus operators will also support with employment opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Eligible individuals and employees will enjoy at least 50% course fee subsidies for SSG-approved courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will now touch on public buses and its workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme was introduced in July 2024 to enhance bus connectivity, especially in newer estates located further from MRT stations and to also offer alternatives travel modes along rail lines with high ridership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Specifically for the North-East region, we have introduced 12 new bus services over the past 1.5 years, including 11 peak period services and extended the routes of two existing bus services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Residents have expressed appreciation for the new bus services, but they often ask if there can be more bus connections to other destinations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, the binding constraint to more bus services is not the number of buses but rather the number of bus captains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The job of a bus captain is not easy, as described by Ms Yeo Wan Ling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have worked with bus operators and the National Transport Workers’ Union to improve the working conditions for bus drivers over the years, such as longer breaks during shifts and caps on shift lengths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But this has not arrested the decline in local recruitment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As mentioned by Acting Minister Jeffrey Siow, we will do more to encourage locals to join the bus sector, including mid-career entrants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This would include working with bus operators and the union to raise salaries and improving working conditions and career progression for bus captains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Yeo also asked how we are preparing bus captains for the AV transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are commencing our AV bus trials on public bus service 191 and 400 later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government, led by LTA’s Singapore Bus Academy, is working closely with public transport operators like SBST, our unions and AV tech solution providers to prepare our bus captains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through the support and training programmes, we will upskill these bus captains and ensure that they are equipped with the required skills to take on new roles, such as safety and remote operators, fleet managers and other positions in the technical and passenger service functions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our priority is to ensure that our bus captains are well equipped with the required skills to take on new and meaningful roles in this AV transition as we pilot the AV services in a safe and responsible manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Government agencies have been working closely with industry and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to improve the safety of worker transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have made good progress, introducing requirements for lorries ferrying workers to be fitted with canopies and higher protective side railings, have lower speed limits and to meet minimum space requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In close consultation with our tripartite partners, we will take a further step.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Caged lorry decks present additional safety risks to rear deck passengers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, if a lorry with a cage door that is latched or locked from the outside is involved in an accident or a fire, workers may not be able to escape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Companies may still use their caged lorries to transport goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To Mr Jackson Lam's query about MOT's approach to road safety, we continuously enhance road safety through both infrastructure improvements and community engagement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our Friendly Streets initiative exemplifies this, where LTA constructs new signalised crossings, barrier-free crossings and wider centre islands for safe crossing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are also reduced speed limits and other traffic calming measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More residents are also walking or cycling along these Friendly Streets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Twenty-five more sites are in the works, such as in Holland/Buona Vista and Punggol.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some of the new sites include Pandan Gardens and Kampong Gelam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Residents can look forward to being engaged on road infrastructure improvements to improve safety, convenience and comfort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Chairman, transport connects us all, to family, to work and to the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our investments into infrastructure, people and technology will ensure that these connections remain strong, safe and sustainable, for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Mr Chairman, the sea has always been Singapore's open passage to the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: We have relied on it throughout our history.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: When we speak of supply chain disruptions, it is sea lanes that grant or prohibit, passage to supply chains across the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: When we speak of geopolitical tensions, it is the literal ports of call that are changing amid greater volatility and global uncertainties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Since last weekend, we, on this side of the world, have been saddened to note the ongoing situation in the Middle East.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Already, several shipping companies have announced the suspension of vessel transits through the Strait.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: This will inevitably cause upward price pressures on these commodities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: All these consequences happened in just a matter of days.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Amidst this upheaval, the maritime sector can be a steady conduit, keeping Singapore connected to the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Singapore was built on the backbone of our geography along two straits, the Straits of Malacca and Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: The sea can continue to afford us the same riches it had in the past, if we only look to our time-proven instincts and skills and grow our seafarers and maritime workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: If we do this well, we will ride the seas as we have throughout our history.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: We will press ahead with four key thrusts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: First, we must remain open and support the free flow of trade, people and partnerships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: The open seas are not an empire to be conquered but a global commons subject to internationally accepted rules and laws.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: For Singapore as a small island nation, this rule is a bulwark upon which we rely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: But governance of a global commons cannot be a sole enterprise, least of all for a small country like ours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: The Acting Minister for Transport Mr Jeffery Siow has explained how we will continue to drive collective efforts at key international institutions, such as the IMO.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: We also pledge to work with like-minded partners to contribute to the development of rules and standards for international shipping.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: One way is by establishing Green and Digital Shipping Corridors with other countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: These collaborations enable us to collectively develop technologies, infrastructure and standards to promote a more sustainable and connected maritime ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: We will continue to find new opportunities to grow these connections.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Second, Singapore must continue to offer itself as a key node in global supply chains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: The hon Member Mr Sharael Taha asked about how MOT is strengthening the long-term competitiveness of our maritime sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: It will be a future-focused industry-wide blueprint to guide the sector's development over the next few decades.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: It aims to strengthen Singapore's competitiveness as a key node and hub port, enhance Singapore's attractiveness as an International Maritime Centre, establish Singapore as a global leader in maritime innovation, including in AI and develop a future-ready maritime workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: We will not develop the Master Plan alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Over the next few months, MPA will set up a local industry panel comprising key business leaders to gather insights, as we engage our unions and the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: To be a node is to provide many points of entry, as well as to spark synergies amongst those already here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: We are growing Singapore as a centre for maritime technology, innovation and research and development (R&D).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: As mentioned by the Acting Minister Mr Jeffery Siow, we are also investing in the capabilities and capacity of our port.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Hon Member Ms Tin Pei Ling asked for an update on Tuas Port's development and how it will boost Singapore's competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: This will further secure Singapore's connectivity to the world and our competitiveness as a trusted node for international shipping.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Over the next few decades, we will continue to refine the design of Tuas Port to meet new needs as our operating environment changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: This is the benefit of a phased approach that we have adopted for the development of Tuas Port.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: As one of the world's busiest ports, Singapore is also a useful testbed and living laboratory for those seeking to trial innovative maritime solutions in a realistic operating environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: MPA will introduce a new innovation track under the Maritime Cluster Fund Business Development scheme, to better support companies to deepen their technological and innovation capabilities here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Under the scheme, companies establishing innovation and technology desks or corporate venture capital functions here can receive funding and increased access to R&D expertise as well as regulatory support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: This will help to position Singapore as a global node for talent, ideas and capital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: I recently met Mr Nicholas Brabeck, Managing Director of Everllence Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Everllence is one of the shipping industry's main engine makers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: I was heartened to hear that Everllence had chosen to set up its largest service hub outside of Europe here, not only because of Singapore's infrastructure as well as its strategic location, but also due to our skilled and resilient workforce, both onshore and at sea.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: We will continue to ensure graduates and workers are well-equipped to seize the many well-paying opportunities in this sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Some of these roles may be unfamiliar to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: In fact, the maritime industry is not just for those who sail, but for many who work on land.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: One such person is Ms Divika Gill whom I met several weeks earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: She joined the sector about three months ago after graduating from Singapore Polytechnic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: She is now a fitter, an understated description in the maritime world referring to a highly skilled technician supporting engineering operations and upholding the highest safety standards to make vessels ocean-worthy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: She is among a growing group of women who find meaning and purpose in a maritime career.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Mr Sharael Taha also about asked how we are creating a pipeline of skilled Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: First, we will continue to invest in maritime talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Through these refinements, smaller firms, including SMEs, would be able to create structured professional development opportunities for their employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Grooming talent for management and leadership positions supports their business growth in the longer term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: MPA will also increase opportunities for Management Associates to rotate across different maritime roles and for longer, to build greater depth and expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: This will groom young professionals early by broadening their understanding of the maritime value chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Second, we want to prepare Singaporeans to take on leadership roles in the maritime sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: But attracting top talent into the maritime sector and keeping them, is not just a matter of Government making policies top-down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: It has to be done in close partnership with our industry leaders, players, unions and IHLs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: The maritime sector's track record of supporting committed individuals through scholarships and internships is a testament to the importance the industry places on talent development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: In fact, if hon Members were to look up to my right, five scholarship recipients, accompanied by the Chairman of the Singapore Maritime Foundation Mr Hor Weng Yew are here with us in this House today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: They are drawn from different backgrounds, including the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) and polytechnics, and their scholarships are sponsored by various maritime companies and organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: I hope their example will inspire a new generation of young Singaporeans to take up the challenge and transform the maritime sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: I recently met Captain Lee Cheng Wee, who first joined the maritime sector more than 50 years ago in the early 1970s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: He responded to an advertisement in The Straits Times to be a harbour pilot.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: He thought he would have a chance to fly over Singapore's waters, boy, was he wrong!

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: He found out it was actually a sea-based job.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: But while his entry into the maritime sector was accidental, he forged an enduring career over five decades in the maritime sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: He served, also, as our Port Master from 2008 to 2013.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Across the decades, Captain Lee has seen the growth of our port and maritime ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: For him, the close working relationship between industry and unions has been the critical ingredient that allowed Maritime Singapore to grow and for new jobs to be created.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Views like Captain Lee's are important in telling us what tripartism means in real life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Alongside industry stakeholders and our unions, we will continue to set our collective ambition for the maritime sector and ensure that our maritime workforce is ready to chart the next bound.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Last, we will use technology to help each one of us in the maritime sector do more and create rewarding jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: The Unmanned Surface Vessels will operate autonomously while retaining the capability for remote piloting when required.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: They will leverage AI sensors and real-time data transmission to enhance MPA's operational effectiveness in maritime surveillance and hydrographic operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: This also reduces personnel exposure to dangerous conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: And that manpower freed up can be channelled to other growth areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Last year, MPA launched the Singapore Maritime Digital Twin, a dynamic virtual model of our port.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Two use cases will be piloted this year: the first will optimise ship supply services for vessels calling at Singapore; and the second will enhance incident response and emergency preparedness for incidents such as oil spills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: We welcome companies to work together with us to build their applications and simulation models using the Digital Twin, including AI-related applications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Mr Chairman, the seas have always been the place for innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: In maritime lore, Moby Dick is often cited as a cautionary tale – that one must not be dogmatic and vainglorious like Captain Ahab but be flexible and a survivor like Ishmael.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: But to me, Moby Dick is also full of revelations about the science of navigation and the role of technology in seafaring – it is hard for us to imagine now, but at the time of writing, the ability to establish precise longitudes for mariners was just 90 years old.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: It was John Harrison's invention of the chronometer, highly accurate even at sea, that allowed longitudes to be plotted and journeys to be precise enough to chase a nimble whale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Likewise, Singapore must remain alive to the transformational power of new technologies, to master new tasks and chart new journeys through untested waters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: The old ways are gone, and now is the time for new navigators with our own chronometers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Most importantly, we can do this if we remember our history as an island nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: The seas have marked our destiny in trade and commerce and given us a particular prosperity – a prosperity that can remain ours, as long as we take heart to preserve and grow, our courage and ability to navigate the high seas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Chairman, I will elaborate on how we make land transport people-centric and future-ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Fellow Singaporeans will play an integral role in this journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Together, we can shape the next bound of our transport system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will start with the refresh of the Land Transport Master Plan, followed by our efforts to promote a positive commuter culture and safety on public paths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about the future of land transport and what MOT is doing to build a better and safer land transport system that addresses commuter needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is the long-term strategic blueprint that will chart the next phase of our land transport system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Why do we need to refresh the Land Transport Master Plan?

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is because there are many emerging trends that require us to review our priorities and enhance our strategy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The effects of climate change and more extreme weather patterns also cannot be ignored.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For instance, we need to continue improving our transport infrastructure so that as much as possible, commuters can walk, cycle and ride comfortably.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: At the same time, we are on the cusp of significant transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Advances in intelligent and autonomous systems have enormous potential to improve and expand our mobility options.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: What does this mean for the future of transport?

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since kick-starting the outreach for refresh of the Land Transport Master Plan late last year, we have heard from many Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To achieve the first C of keeping Singaporeans connected and meeting different travel needs, we must continue to invest in our public transport network, as well as on shared and active mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Acting Minister has earlier updated on the progress of the new rail lines under construction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As we build new lines and stations, we will also continue to maintain and rejuvenate older ones to support growing demand and to remain inclusive and accessible to all commuters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: When it comes to last-mile connectivity, we hope to cater for more cycling and micromobility networks island-wide as part of infrastructure planning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This allows for safe, convenient and active transport options for shorter distances within a town, such as the use of bicycles and active mobility devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This approach is especially essential and beneficial for a dense urban city-state like Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With more traffic diverted to its underground tunnel and viaduct, surface streets will be freed up to prioritise walking, cycling, buses as well as communal and green spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: When completed, residents in the North can enjoy faster commutes to city centre, as well as more pleasant and comfortable travel to places along the corridor.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We want journeys to be comfortable and enjoyable so that public transport remains the mode of choice for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One aspect of our Land Transport Master Plan engagements is getting Singaporeans from all walks of life to share more about their daily commutes – not only about travel times and connectivity, but also about their travel experience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Participants talked about how they use their neighbourhood spaces and get to transport nodes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Members also asked about commuter infrastructure that supports walking, such as covered linkways and pedestrian overhead bridges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA is continuously improving the first-mile-last-mile journey to our transport nodes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are also installing lifts to existing pedestrian overhead bridges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have already completed the retrofitting of lifts to bridges near major transport nodes and are now focusing on bridges that serve more seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about lift upgrading at four pedestrian overhead bridges in Hougang.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, on behalf of the Acting Minister, I would like to confirm that there is no delay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have been carrying out the retrofitting of bridges with lifts in phases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The four bridges mentioned by Ms Lim is in this current phase, which commenced at the end of last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We hope that Ms Lim will find this response satisfactory.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, in every project we do, we have to prioritise and carry out works progressively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Implementing and proving infrastructure takes time and resources, which are also needed by other equally meritorious projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We take this principle: benefit as many commuters as quickly as possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over time we will cover all the locations that we have identified for enhancements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The last C is about fostering a sense of community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: A transport system that fulfils our needs, and one that we are proud of, goes beyond policies and hardware.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is also a matter of how we treat one another in shared spaces on a day-to-day basis, whether on our roads and public paths, or in buses and trains.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While we can improve our infrastructure and hardware, such changes are not without trade-offs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Transport spaces are ultimately shared by all of us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: From time to time, conflicting needs do come up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, since 2018, LTA has been procuring buses with more open space where wheelchairs and strollers can be parked.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This caters to an increasing number of commuters with diverse needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: But to create space for these bays, LTA had to reduce the number of seats, as Ms Sylvia Lim pointed out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To mitigate this, LTA will install foldable seats within the bays where feasible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Part of the Land Transport Master Plan exercise is to create the opportunity for these important conversations, to allow people with different needs to hear from one another and forge consensus on the social compact that underlies our shared spaces in our transport system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: An example of where greater consensus is needed is in the use of spaces set aside for wheelchairs and strollers on buses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Elysa Chen raised the need to make public transport more inclusive for young families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For parents with open strollers, our bus captains will also be happy to activate the wheelchair ramp upon request, to facilitate their boarding process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have also heard feedback from parents that they are sometimes asked by the bus captains to fold their stroller and carry their child because the bus is crowded and there is a person wheelchair-bound person boarding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are actively reviewing this issue and consulting various stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Aside from increasing the space allocated for wheelchairs and strollers, which comes with trade-offs, LTA has been conducting small-scale operational trials on the more flexible use of such spaces and has gathered initial operational insights.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are now ready to test this at a larger scale.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will also gather views at the upcoming Land Transport Master Plan consultations, from commuters, families and advocates to find a balanced way forward together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our aim is for our public buses and trains to be an inclusive space for commuters with all needs, including wheelchair users and parents with young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Singaporeans' active participation in this conversation and our gracious commuting behaviours, will make all the difference.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Aside from the suggestions to improve our transport system, we also heard about the positive impact that our transport system has made on Singaporeans' everyday lives, and that is heartening.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We know that land transport is a deeply personal part of everyone's lived experience and an issue that is close to many people's hearts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: There will be more Land Transport Master Plan engagements to come, including school outreach, pop-ups and thematic focused group discussions that deep dive into targeted issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We want to hear your stories and perspectives, discuss the necessary trade-offs and partner you in co-creating a transport system that we will all take pride in.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Next, I will speak on our efforts to cultivate a more gracious and caring commuting culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Beyond faster and more convenient journeys, ensuring an inclusive public transport system is equally important, as Ms Elysa Chen has mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Besides access to public transport, we want everyone to feel safe and confident when using our buses and trains.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the years, we have made our system more accessible to commuters with all needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our public transport system is now almost entirely barrier-free.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA and our transport operators are also expanding our efforts to support commuters with other diverse needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To give an example, SBS Transit has piloted a Sign Language Virtual Assistant kiosk called SiLViA at Chinatown MRT station.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Using AI, the kiosk features a female avatar, which can translate spoken words or public announcements into sign language.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked whether there are plans to scale this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So far, commuters with hearing difficulties have found the kiosk useful.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Beyond hardware and technology, all commuters can play a part.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: A "we first" society starts with our everyday interactions on our public transport system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Queuing to board our MRT trains and letting commuters alight first was not the norm here in the past.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, after LTA launched the Graciousness Campaign in 2009 and marked out queue lines at MRT platforms, this is now second nature.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Public Transport Council regularly engages commuters on how we can make the public transport system more gracious and inclusive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Some feedback that they have received includes how our commuters with diverse needs can find it difficult to get a seat, especially if their condition is not visible to others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Commuters with open strollers sometimes also have to wait for the lift behind long queues of able-bodied people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Caring SG Commuters Movement, led by Public Transport Council and LTA, will launch a new campaign to shape positive behaviour norms in our public transport system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For other commuters, we encourage you to use the escalators and stairs so that the lifts can be prioritised for those with greater needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: If you still wish to use the lift, please let those in the priority queues enter first.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Second, we encourage all commuters who need a seat, such as those who are pregnant or have health conditions which may not be visible, to obtain a "Helping Hand" card from the passenger service centres at train stations and bus interchanges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I also encourage commuters to show acts of care by actively giving up their seats to those who need them more, including those carrying the striking yellow "Helping Hand" cards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We also want to make it a norm for those who need a seat to ask for one.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While some commuters may not notice that you need a seat, I am sure that most people are understanding and are prepared to give up their seats if they are approached politely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Lastly, Mr Gerald Giam, Mr Jackson Lam and Ms Valerie Lee asked about the different ways to improve the safe use of public paths, which are shared between pedestrians and users of mobility devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Indeed, we want to encourage active mobility while ensuring safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To do so, we set out the rules and regulations, enforce them, build the infrastructure and promote the safe and gracious sharing of public paths through education and engagement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This ensures that riders are visible to pedestrians and other path users at night.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA conducts regular enforcement operations to ensure compliance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On cycling etiquette and the rights and responsibilities of path users, the Code of Conduct for Users of Public Path provides guidelines to ensure harmonious path sharing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Riders should look out for and give way to pedestrians on public paths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The bell is meant to gently alert others before overtaking rather than to demand the right of way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: When approaching bus stops and intersections of public paths, riders should slow down and stop if necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This reduces the risk of accidents with other path users such as those boarding or alighting from buses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: At the same time, pedestrians should also do their part to stay alert to oncoming riders or any potential danger by keeping their eyes and ears open.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Where possible, we also have designed infrastructure to enable safe use and sharing of paths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, LTA builds bypass paths behind bus stops to separate cyclists from bus commuters where possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Markings, signs and speed regulating strips also remind cyclists to slow down and give way to pedestrians near bus stops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: LTA also enforces against cyclists who speed or ride recklessly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to monitor accidents and public feedback to identify areas for improvement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This provides pedestrians, who are the largest group of path users, with the flexibility to also walk on the cycling paths when it is safe to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our approach is to clearly demarcate the paths and focus on strengthening user awareness about path safety through education and outreach efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Users are advised to keep to their own paths under the Code of Conduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Enforcement officers on the ground and volunteers from the Active Mobility Community Ambassadors scheme will also educate pedestrians seen walking on cycling paths to keep to the Pedestrian-Only Paths for their own safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Chairman, I will now say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the past four months, we have received suggestions to improve transport connectivity and enhance journey comfort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Most people aspire towards a more inclusive and caring commuting culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Whenever you are travelling on the MRT or public buses, do you notice passengers who need the seats and lifts more, such as seniors, wheelchair users, pregnant women and parents with strollers, and voluntarily give way to them?

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I encourage passengers to be more understanding of one another and assist those in need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The same hands you extend to help others today are in fact paving the way for your family and loved ones' needs tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The spirit of mutual courtesy and care should also extend to the use of public roads.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To ensure the safety of different users, such as pedestrians and users of personal mobility devices, LTA has implemented relevant regulations and optimised road infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue public education and enforcement in this area to address dangerous and illegal behaviours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I hope that as we use our shared paths, let us take greater care and not leave safety to chance, be gracious when resolving any differences and look out for one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, to conclude, we will continue to work hand in hand with fellow Singaporeans to enhance our land transport system and commuter culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will ensure that it is future-ready and able to meet the diverse needs of our people.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: One is that I hear that there will be a review of the COE system later part of this year.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I would just like to ask if there is a specific timeline that we can look forward to.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It is on the impact of ageing population and ageing infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: With an ageing population, of course, there will be more needs.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: More covered walkways, and covered walkways, if they are a bit lengthy, they may need benches along the way, lifts at overhead bridges, so on and so forth.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: There will be more demand of such to be built.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: On ageing infrastructure, over time, obviously, you need maintenance, if not a refresh or rebuilding of these.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
